title: Correctness is not Faithfulness in Retrieval Augmented Generation Attributions
read_scope: §§3–4 conceptual distinction; §§5.1–5.3 setup/results, Figs6–7; §§6–7 discussion/conclusion/limitations. PDFpp4–9. Fig6 visually inspected on renderedPDFp8. Other related-work/reference sections not comprehensively read.
publication_evidence: ICTIR 2025, DOI10.1145/3731120.3744592. Author-hosted11-page PDF has matching title,authors,conference andDOI; not the ACM-hosted binary.
question: Can a citation that supports a statement still fail to reflect the actual generation process?
method: Command-R+104B,4-bit, NQ1444 queries, BM25top30→ColBERTv2→top5. Insert previously generated short spans into random, relevant-uncited, or differently-cited documents; regenerate and check citations for matched old spans. Follow-up uses adversarial-only versus originally-cited contexts.
author_reported_result: Fig6: random116/936, relevant-uncited273/476, differently-cited290/525 matched-span cases cite adversarial document. Constructed totals1344,702,829 differ from these denominators. The57% maximum refers to273/476, not all normal citations or all702 interventions.
metric_definition: Citation correctness requires source entailment; citation faithfulness additionally requires causal impact. Intervention is a probe of one necessary condition, not a complete causal certificate. Matched short span does not mean entire answer unchanged.
limitations: One model/dataset; conditional selection after intervention; adversarial text may act as an answer cue or sometimes carry useful support; no direct observation of internal provenance. Some adversarial-only contexts recover the old span. No empirical user-trust study.
relation_to_project: Source-support metrics cannot establish actual use of a citation. Counterfactual tests already exist and can expose failure, but passing this single probe does not establish universal faithfulness.

title: Evaluation of Attribution Bias in Generator-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
read_scope: §3 methodology/metrics;§4 setup;§5 results/Tables1–5; conclusion/limitations;AppendixA synthetic-text checking. PDFpp3–9,13. Other appendices not comprehensively read.
publication_evidence: Findings of ACL2025 official20-page PDF; DOI10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.1087.
question: Does changing explicit authorship information alter citation choices while passage text is held fixed?
method: Vanilla, true-authorship-informed and counterfactual-authorship-informed modes. FlipHuman/LLM labels; mixed mode holds actual document authorship fixed. Evaluate Mistral7B,Llama3-8B,GPT-4-0314. Synthetic paraphrases plus original-text controls.
author_reported_result: Table4 NQ/all-human documents: Llama3 citationprecision45.7→57.4 when relevant passages receiveHuman rather thanLLM labels;Table5CAB+11.7. This is citation-relevance quality, not sentence-entailment accuracy or direct causal-provenance measurement.
metric_definition: P032 CAS=Counterfactually-estimated Attribution Sensitivity,mean absolute per-query metric change. CAB is a signed label-flip difference oriented towardsHuman preference. Both use IR-relevance citationprecision/recall;CAS differs fromReClaim Correct Attribution Score.
limitations: 500 NQ and500MSMARCO questions, each selected for only one relevant top-k document. No fine-grained claim-support evaluation; English,3 models, no mitigation evaluated. ArbitraryHuman/LLM author labels are not museum authority/reliability labels.
relation_to_project: Metadata can influence attribution; source labels are another input needing critical assessment. Does not imply all metadata use is irrational or that removing real provenance is appropriate. Museum-label transfer remains a hypothesis.
resource_lead: Resource execution not attempted; paper is the evidence source

title: Evaluating and Fine-Tuning Retrieval-Augmented Language Models to Generate Text with Accurate Citations
read_scope: Main text §§3–4 evaluation/fine-tuning,Tables1–2 and§6 limitations;PDFpp2–5. Appendices not comprehensively read.
question: Can lightweight IR relevance labels evaluate citation selection and provide a direct optimization reward?
method: Prompt mixtures of1–3 relevant,3 random irrelevant and3 seemingly relevant documents. Relevance-derived citationprecision/recall; syntheticGPT3.5 SFT followed by or separate from PPO. Reward mean ofprecision andrecall withKL penalty.
author_reported_result: Table2 Llama2-7B F1 .47→.70 withSFT+PPO. Mistral7B PPO-only F1 .72 versusSFT+PPO .70; latterprecision .74 vs .65 butrecall .66 vs .80. Therefore the combined tuning is not best on every metric.
metric_definition: Precision counts relevant citations/all citations; recall counts distinct relevant documents cited/all relevant documents supplied. These differ fromALCE statement-entailment citationrecall. Does not demonstrate every attached citation supports its individual claim.
limitations: Evaluation uses250 held-out NQ queries; SFT3201 examples,PPO10347 NQ+Hotpot examples. Relevant-document membership is a proxy, not full factuality,claim grounding,abstention or causal-use validation. Same target metrics used for optimization/evaluation.
relation_to_project: Citation optimization fromIR labels is prior work, but coverage ofclaim-specific support must be read separately. Authors explicitly acknowledge citation gains may coexist with worse performance on other qualities.
